summary: The section 6 event engine and the rules R1-R20 are implemented in Sim/*.cs, plus the scripted controllers of 5.6. Simulation owns the round state and the tick skeleton (BeforeTick, steps 1-3, Time = Tick / TickRate, EndTick and the partial last tick, Ended, RoundResult, RankOf with competition ranking fixed for an eliminated player when its Step returns, StateHash FNV-1a, AreaPercent, the Debug* hooks with the exact state of 10.0 item 4). EventResolver follows section 6 to the letter: controllers polled first, R3 turn, R4 Arena.Step, visit lists from GridRaster.TraverseFrom(Cell), the tick-u convention with uTrailEnd and L_i(u), candidates computed from the live state (home transitions from the visit list plus the state check at uCur, cuts by Trail.FirstContact with the full tick segment, closed-form spark catch with the epsilon shift u_c = max(uCur, u0 + eps / dt), lasso as the first VALID crossing of Trail.SelfCrossings + LoopPolygon + IsValidPocket, pickup by contact intervals [in, out) with the n(u) == 1 rule, TimeUp), grouping by EventEpsilonSeconds with uG, group time for Time / TimeCut / EliminatedAt, own u for geometry, the cell-count snapshot, the fixed order a-g with re-validation, the R18 conflict rule, stolen home cells (R9, R18b), zero-cell eliminations, idempotent elimination with DistanceHome before Neutralize, Kills credited to dead attackers, EventCapHits, the round end freeze, end-of-tick appends and closed-form S. Capture is LoopErase.Erase(trail + crossing point) then CaptureSolver.Compute with the pending pocket. RingSpawner handles ForcedRingPos, 200 seeded tries with the 100 near-human tries (6 to 22 u), IsNeutralDisc(RingClearance) and RingMinHeadDistance. 55 tests (45 Rules incl. every 10.1 rule id, 10 Scenario tests S1-S6 at 30 / 60 / 144 Hz with identical outcomes, invariants and EventCapHits == 0 checked after every tick, determinism by StateHash). Result in the project: 51 / 55 green, full Core suite 210 / 214. The 4 red tests are S5 and S6 and they fail ONLY because of a defect in Geo.ProperIntersect (A1, contract 5.1): its 1e-12 dead zone excludes a segment START near the line but not a segment END, so a self crossing that lands within 1e-12 u short of the old segment at a tick end is counted by neither tick, and LoopErase misses the same configuration (R8: an uncharged self loop gets captured). The 10.0 protocol puts every axis-aligned self crossing on a tick boundary, so this happens on roughly half of the lattice crossings. With the one-line-block patch given under needs applied to Geo.cs in a scratch copy, the whole Core suite is 214 / 214 green, the lasso fires at the same instant at 30 / 60 / 144 Hz and captures are identical across rates. Engine cost (dotnet Debug): about 20 us per tick with 4 players trailing on 1800-point trails and repeated self crossings; returns cost one CaptureSolver call each.
api_additions: WaypointController.ReachRadius: public const double 0.3 (the 5.6 reach distance).

WaypointController.NextIndex(int playerIndex): index of the waypoint that player currently steers to (== waypoint count when a non-looping list is done). The controller keeps per-player progress, so one instance can serve several players.

WaypointController behaviour addition: with a finite turn rate a waypoint within 2 r of the head (r = PawnSpeed / TurnRateRad, 0.64 u at 540 deg/s) that is behind the head also counts as reached, so a waypoint approached from the side is never orbited forever. Inactive with TurnRateDeg = 0 (all scripted tests).

No public member was added to Simulation, SimView or the data types. EventResolver and RingSpawner stay internal; Simulation only gained internal plumbing (Controllers, PlayerArray, HumanIndex, ForcedRingPos, EliminatedRank, Emit, EndRound, internal setters of Ring / NextRingTime / EventCapHits).

Test side (assembly PainterIO.Tests.EditMode, namespace PainterIO.Tests): public static class SimTestKit for every agent: Config(rate, lassoSpawns) with TurnRateDeg 0; SimBuilder (AddRect / AddDisc / AddIdle players with their own territory, HumanIndex, ForcedRingPos); EventLog (events with the Tick that raised them, Of / Single / First / Dump); AssertInvariants (the 10.1 invariant list + EventCapHits == 0); StepN / RunUntilTime / RunUntil with invariants every tick; CrossRate + Outcome + AssertSameOutcome (10.0 item 3 at 30 / 60 / 144 Hz); Legs(heading, length) schedules on 1/6 s; FillRect / RectCellCount / CellIndex / OwnerAt; PocketScenario (the S5 / S6 lasso path) and PocketReturnTime; IdleCorners.
contract_issues: 5.1 Geo.ProperIntersect (blocking, see needs): the dead zone is one-sided. A segment whose START a0 lies within 1e-12 |b1 - b0| of the old segment's line is rejected, but a segment whose END a1 lies within that band on the near side computes ta = 1 + O(1e-16) and is rejected by ta <= 1. A crossing that lands within 1e-12 u of the line at a segment end (rounding of accumulated motion) is therefore lost by both segments. It hits the engine (Trail.SelfCrossings: no lasso, no LassoCrossNoCharge) and LoopErase (the loop at that vertex is not erased, so an ordinary return captures a self loop, violating R8; the lasso point X = Lerp(p0, p1, u) also lies on the old segment's line up to rounding). Measured on the S5 path: the charged lasso fired at 3.5 s at 60 Hz, 5.0 s at 30 Hz and 4.1667 s at 144 Hz, and the uncharged 30 Hz return captured the self loop (1886 cells instead of 1358).

10.0 items 1-2 interact with that defect: with whole-unit legs (switch times on 1/6 s) and axis-aligned legs on cell-center lines (0.125 u apart = 3 ticks at 144 Hz), EVERY axis-aligned self crossing happens exactly at a tick boundary at 144 Hz (and at 30 / 60 Hz for whole-unit offsets). So the protocol puts every scripted lasso exactly where the dead-zone defect bites; the probe's scripted demo lasso (18.2) will be just as exposed. Once Geo is fixed this becomes harmless (verified).

5.5 / 3.2 player count: the round has controllers.Length players. SimSetup.PlayerCount and SimConfig.PlayerCount are not used to size the round; the cloned Config.PlayerCount is set to controllers.Length so views and bots read the right value. The SimConfig passed in is cloned (a caller reusing one config object for several rounds cannot leak changes into a running round). A null controller keeps its player's heading.

Section 6 step a, stolen home cells: read literally ('every alive Home player whose current cell is not its own starts an exit'), a home player whose natural exit falls inside the same group window would be reported as TerritoryStolen (with no taker). The engine applies the step-a exit only when the current cell at uG was taken by one of this group's applied captures (Other = that returner); any other home player on a non-own cell necessarily has its own exit candidate in the group, and step f applies it at its exact crossing point.

Section 6 step c re-validation also requires the victim's Trail.Version to equal the version the cut was computed on: a victim that returned and was made to exit again in step a of the same group (R18b) has a new trail, and the old s_cut would point into it.

Round end inside a tick (LastSurvivor / AllEliminated at uG < uEnd): the event loop stops and step 3 freezes the state at uG (positions, current cells, trail ends and spark S evaluated at uG), so the final state satisfies the invariants; Tick still advances by one and Time follows Tick. RoundResult.EndTime = the group time, except TimeUp where it is RoundDuration exactly. The ring spawner does not run once Ended.

Eliminated players (contract silent): Pos and Cell are set to the head at the elimination instant (own u), so views can place the splash; Home is set to true (the trail is empty), which keeps 'trail empty iff home' true for every player; Alive = false is the flag to test.

Construction (contract silent): a player whose start cell is not its own (custom SimSetup.Territory only) starts trailing from its head without an Exit event, so Home == (owner(Cell) == Id) holds from the first frame.

Section 6 step 3 ring spawn: the spawner runs with the end-of-tick time, so the ring appears in the Step after which Time >= NextRingTime (R15b 'first tick with Time >= 15 s': after Step 900 at 60 Hz, RingSpawned.Time = 15.0 = Ring.SpawnTime). Random candidates must keep the whole ring disc inside the arena (SignedDistance <= -(ArenaMargin + RingRadius)), so every ring is visible and reachable by a head; ForcedRingPos skips every check.

Debug hooks: they raise no events (LastEvents are only the events of a Step); a view must read Sim.Ring after DebugPlaceRing, which places or moves the ring with SpawnTime = Time. DebugForceCut is also a no-op when the victim is home or eliminated, credits CutsMade to the attacker as a real cut would, and accepts attacker -1 (nobody credited, no Kills). DebugSetTrail requires at least 2 points and clears any spark and pocket (a new exit).

SimEvent.Margin is clamped at 0: the grouping rule (u - uMin) dt <= eps can let a return up to 2 eps after the catch root win (R13 says t_r < t_c + eps); the difference is 1e-7 s and the contract's grouping is kept as written, but the margin of such a return would be a few 1e-8 s negative.

SimView.SparkCatchEta = (Trail.Length - Spark.S) / (SparkSpeed - PawnSpeed), clamped at 0, +inf without a spark (assumes the head keeps moving at PawnSpeed; a head held at the border is caught sooner). StateHash hashes more than the minimum list: Tick, cells, per player Pos / Cell / flags (Alive, Home, Charged, has spark) / heading / trail points (all rounded to 1e-9) / spark S / pocket count, then the ring position.

10.1 S6 asks for 'SparkCaught time = t_cut + (L(t_c) - s_cut) / SparkSpeed', which is the closed form itself (tautological). The S6 test also asserts the independent arc-based value t_cut + (L(t_cut) - s_cut) / (SparkSpeed - PawnSpeed), with a cut whose straight distance to the head (5.83 u) is far below half the arc distance (20 u).

failing: S5_ChargedLassoScoreRisesOnlyAtTheReturnByAtLeastThePocket (Geo.ProperIntersect dead zone: the lasso at t = 3.5 s is missed at 30 / 144 Hz)
S5_CaughtWithAPendingPocketThePocketVanishesAndRivalCellsStay (same cause: event sequences differ across tick rates)
S6_SameTrajectoryWithoutChargeNoPocketAndTheLoopIsNotCaptured (same cause: missed crossings, and LoopErase keeps the loop at 30 Hz)
S6_FigureEightChaseFollowsTheArcInPassingOrder (same cause: the figure-8 crossing at t = 16/6 s is missed)

open_issues: The 4 S5 / S6 tests stay red until Geo.ProperIntersect gets the symmetric dead zone (needs). Verified in a scratch copy of the project with only that patch: the full Core suite (A1 + A2 + A3 + A4 tests) is 214 / 214 green.

Unity EditMode was not run by A4 (the task did not require Unity). The tests use only NUnit 3.5 API (Test, TestCase, Assert.That with Is.EqualTo / Within / LessThan / GreaterThan / LessThanOrEqualTo / GreaterThanOrEqualTo, AreEqual, AreSame, IsTrue / IsFalse / IsNull / IsNotNull, Throws, Fail), value tuples and 'using static'. RulesTests.cs, ScenarioTests.cs and SimTestKit.cs get their .meta files on the next Unity run; Gate A should confirm the counts in Unity.

Flicker returns: a head moving along a diagonal edge of its own territory alternates own / neutral cells because of the stair notches left by the 4-adjacency Rim (A2's contract_issues). Each flicker exit is harmless (its trail stays inside HeadGrace), but each return is a full CaptureSolver call. A looped diagonal waypoint path produced about 12 returns per second per player, and the dotnet Debug tick average rose to 283 us (captures dominate). Without returns the engine costs about 20 us per tick with 4 trailing players on 1800-point trails. Bots that hug their edges (A5) could trigger this; an 8-adjacency rim would remove most notches (user decision, A2's suggestion).
A5 (bots) had not landed when this report was written: the 50-round bot test is the real end-to-end performance check of the engine.
R1 / R15: the random ring spawner never places a ring within ArenaMargin + RingRadius (1.05 u) of the rim; ForcedRingPos and DebugPlaceRing can place it anywhere.
needs: Geo.ProperIntersect (Core/Math/Geo.cs, owner A1 foundation; contract 5.1) must treat the END of the moving segment with the same 1e-12 band as its start. Minimal failing test (exact positions of R10's path at 60 Hz, ticks 99 and 100; a crossing must be counted by exactly one of two consecutive segments): var o0 = new Vec2d(1.0, 0.0625); var o1 = new Vec2d(1.1, 0.0625); bool k = Geo.ProperIntersect(new Vec2d(1.0625, 0.16250000000000017), new Vec2d(1.0625, 0.06250000000000017), o0, o1, out _, out _); bool k1 = Geo.ProperIntersect(new Vec2d(1.0625, 0.06250000000000017), new Vec2d(1.0625, -0.03749999999999984), o0, o1, out _, out _); Assert.AreEqual(1, (k ? 1 : 0) + (k1 ? 1 : 0)); -- today both are false (k: ta = 1.0000000000000004; k1: a0 inside the band). Proposed patch, replacing the final 'return ta > 0.0 && ta <= 1.0 && tb >= 0.0 && tb < 1.0;': if (ta > 1.0) { double w1x = b0.X - a1.X, w1y = b0.Y - a1.Y; if (Math.Abs(w1x * dby - w1y * dbx) > 1e-12 * lenB) return false; ta = 1.0; tb = ((a1.X - b0.X) * dbx + (a1.Y - b0.Y) * dby) / (lenB * lenB); } return ta > 0.0 && tb >= 0.0 && tb < 1.0; -- i.e. an end point inside the band counts as reaching the line AT a1 (ta = 1, so SelfCrossing.Point = b and LoopErase takes x = p exactly), while the next segment starting there is still excluded by the a0 rule: exactly once. Evidence: with this patch in a scratch copy, all 214 Core tests pass (incl. every A1 Geo test, A3's LoopErase / SelfCrossings tests and S5 / S6), and on the S5 path all three crossings fire at 3.5, 25/6 and 5.0 s at 30, 60 and 144 Hz with identical captures (2023 cells charged, 1358 uncharged; the uncharged self loop stays neutral).

Contract 5.1 text (user / contract owner): add to the ProperIntersect definition 'a1 within the same 1e-12 |b1 - b0| band of the line counts as reaching it at a1 (ta = 1)', so the half-open rule holds under rounding.
